tag: Episode 46 · The Eclipse of Every Sky
title: The Eclipse of Every Sky

beats.t: Beyond the door was no floor. Black panels formed only where they stepped, vanishing when they lifted a foot.
There was no up or down. Far away floated a single black sun. It swallowed light instead of giving it.
The Void. A place that admits anything because it's empty. I never imagined the inside of my palm looked like this.
Thinking we're inside someone else's palm feels really weird.
Don't step on the palm lines. If my love line breaks, you're responsible, Moka.
No one laughed. Any laughter was sucked toward the black sun the moment it emerged.
It eats sound too?
Everything. That's why we can't stay long.
Yeoni took the notebook from their pocket. The first line had faded a little. They traced over it with a finger.
[ Neo · Cat, then human · Silver hair · Lots of scolding · Socks · On my side ]
We heard his voice through the door. Telling me to match my socks. He's somewhere here.
Then finding him comes first. Fighting comes afterward.
We'll probably end up fighting while we look. We always do.
The ground shook. Things fell between the black panels. Huge things. Fragments the size of buildings.
The star palace of twelve palaces fell upside down. Its rooftop stars went dark one by one.
The observatory skyship slid down with torn sails. The sky of twelve houses crumpled like a folded map.
The bell of the twenty-seven lunar mansions rang once. Then the entire temple tilted toward the black sun.
Cards from the corridor scattered like a blizzard. Finally, five islands from the sea tumbled down, small as toys.
That's our island! The Island of Expression!
All five skies are collapsing here. Black Moon left the door open and waited for us to enter.
It's destroying everything because we came in?
Not destroying. Eating. Once it's eaten everything, only one sky will remain here. That one.
Yundal pointed at the black sun. Fallen fragments orbited it, disappearing one by one.
Eyes appeared in the black sun. Not one. One for each fallen sky. Five in all.
Welcome. I have waited, vessel.
Names rose around the sun. Names Yeoni had heard along the way: black Obstruction Transformation. The dark moon Lilith. Rahu's head and Ketu's tail. The collapsing Tower.
The same thing all along. Wearing a different name in each sky.
The more names, the better. Each meal added one.
Hundreds of black hands stretched from beneath the sun. A person's name tag hung from every finger.
Give those names back. Not one belongs to you.
Rainwater, always demanding the return of others' things. Yet you never once protected your own.
Seo Hanbi tightened her grip on the umbrella. She didn't answer. Instead, she stepped forward, in front of Yeoni.
Before fighting, let us trade. I am fair. I taught the ledger-keeper that myself.
A black hand lowered before Moka. A little stage opened on its palm: the noon stage with the sun overhead, packed with an audience.
Ember. I will return every song on your island. The applause too. In exchange, withdraw.
We got our songs back by singing them ourselves. Not from you.
Moka knocked the stage away with the back of his paw. It scattered into ash.
And applause isn't borrowed. It's received. If you don't know the difference, don't perform.
Fortune-teller. Don't you want to go home? I will return your hour. The Hour of the Rabbit. And your name.
A clock appeared on the palm. Its hands trembled near five twenty. Yundal couldn't take his eyes from them.
Is that real?
Yundal.
Yundal reached out. Just before his fingertips touched the clock, he stopped. His gloved fingers trembled in midair.
Even if it's real, I won't take it. If I do, I go home. But Yeoni stays here.
And I found my own hour through birth-time rectification. No reason to receive it from you.
A black hand moved before Seo Hanbi. A rainy bus stop rested on its palm. The bus stop of the first spring. An envelope lay on the bench.
Rainwater. I will let you return. To that day, that bus stop. This time I won't interfere. The girl, the envelope, the sea—all yours.
Seo Hanbi stopped breathing. The rain sounded too real. She could read the envelope: Go to the sea together.
Back to that spring.
Hanbi.
Yeoni said only her name. Neither stopping nor holding her. Letting her choose.
If I return to that spring, the umbrella this spring's Yeoni gave me disappears. The one with three layers of tape.
I'm not going. I'll repay what I owe in this spring.
Seo Hanbi covered the bus stop with her hand, quietly, as though setting down something held for a long time. The little bus stop dissolved into rainwater.
Every one of you, so dull. Then I will ask the vessel directly.
The last hand opened before Yeoni. Neo lay curled on its palm, eyes closed, body cloudy as glass. It was impossible to tell whether he breathed.
What you have forgotten. You cannot even remember its name, can you? Empty yourself and I'll return it. Become my vessel, and it can remain inside you too. Forever.
Yeoni looked at that face. No name, no memory came. Only their palm grew hot.
Gold seeped from Yeoni's left hand, where the thread from beneath the tower had entered. The light stretched toward the black hand, then gathered in their palm again.
Ah.
What is this? Why is my hand hot?
For the first time, Black Moon's voice wavered. All five eyes turned toward Yeoni's palm.
So there it was. The piece I couldn't finish eating.
Hundreds of black hands lunged at once. At Yeoni. More precisely, at their left hand.
Yeoni, back!
Seo Hanbi opened the umbrella. Rain poured beneath it, standing as a wall that blocked the hands. Whenever a finger touched the rain, a name tag fell away.
Don't need matches. My fire comes from my mouth!
Moka drew a great breath and shouted. Rap. Rhythm and lyrics both a mess. Still, sparks flew from his voice. Several hands scorched and recoiled.
I'll eat them. Move a little.
Yundal removed his glove and held out his palm. Hands streamed into it. His face went white. The circle of the Void spread to his wrist.
Stop! It's growing!
That's what this hand is for.
But the hands were endless. The rain wall thinned. Moka's voice cracked. Yundal's knees buckled.
Why resist? Surrender one vessel and it all ends.
Yeoni held their golden left hand against their chest. If they gave up even this, the road back to that person would vanish. They didn't know why, but they knew that.
Yundal. This light. What is it?
Gyeong. Mr. Cat's Metal. A piece remained inside your vessel.
Your Four Pillars have all five energies by nature. Wood, Fire, Earth, Water, and that Metal.
Yundal indicated Seo Hanbi, Moka, himself, then Yeoni.
And we happen to have all five here. Fire, Earth, Water, Wood. Metal in your hand.
If we gather the five energies...
An eclipse forms when Sun and Moon overlap. If the five energies make one circuit, that overlap comes undone. Probably.
Why so many probablys?!
At that instant, the rain wall tore. A black hand slipped through and seized not Yeoni, but Seo Hanbi's wrist. Her right wrist, at the ring scar.
Then I shall eat Water first. Remove one of five, and nothing turns.
Seo Hanbi was dragged toward the black sun. The umbrella fell from her hand. Its taped handle rolled over the black panels.
Hanbi!
Yeoni didn't think. They picked up the rolling umbrella and ran. Their golden left hand gripped the umbrella; their right caught Seo Hanbi's other hand.
Let go! You'll be dragged in too!
No. You chose me earlier. This time, I choose.
The two were dragged together. Moka grabbed Yeoni's bag strap; Yundal grabbed Moka's waist. The four hung in a line as the black sun drew closer.
What kind of tug-of-war is this?! Our side's too weak!
Tug-of-war ends with one pull all at once. Not yet.
Then gold flared once more from Yeoni's left hand. Along the umbrella handle, along Seo Hanbi's wrist. At its touch, the black fingers flinched and loosened a little.
Give me that light. It was mine to begin with.
Don't be ridiculous. It's written in my note. On my side. The person on my side isn't yours.
